title: Elsa Morante's birth chart
metaDescription: Elsa Morante's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 25.1° Leo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 25.1° Leo, in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 25.1° into Leo — the third decan, which the old scheme hands to Mars. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 2.3° Virgo, Venus was at 7.1° Virgo, Mars was at 20.2° Virgo. Read together: thought with its feet on the ground; attraction that grows by reliability; effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Mercury at right angles from Saturn, 1.1° off exact. Right angles are where the scheme puts its grit. A square asks two functions to work in a mode neither would have chosen. Behind it, Venus square Jupiter at 1.1°, and Mercury sextile Pluto at 2.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Jupiter opposes Saturn while both square Mercury. A t-square aims the whole axis at its apex planet; the tradition reads it as the chart’s standing assignment. The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Read against the old dignities, five placements stand out. The Sun in Leo at 25.1° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; the Moon in Scorpio at 10.3° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Mercury in Virgo at 2.3° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Venus in Virgo at 7.1° is in fall; Jupiter in Sagittarius at 5.9° is in domicile. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 3 earth, 3 air, 2 fire, 2 water by element and 6 mutable, 3 fixed, 1 cardinal by modality. Earth counts what remains: the built, the kept, the finished. Promise weighs less than delivery. Mercury and Uranus were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Scorpio for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.1° between midnight and midnight. The sign survives the missing hour; the degree does not, and is given as a reference rather than a fact. At the noon reference it stands at 10.3°.
